title: REVOLUTION MEN'S LEAGUE | WEEK 1 RECAP
content: Week 1 was a wild welcome back to the hardwood for the Revolution Men's League. Sub JJ and Josh Carter both erupted for 32 points apiece, Green held off a hard-charging White team down the stretch, and Pink stormed all the way back from an eight-point halftime hole to steal one on the road. Let's get into the action.

games.text: Gray controlled the tempo from the opening tip. Gray set the pace early, leaning on Matt Spear's inside scoring and Tommy Brockmyre's activity around the rim to build some separation. John Helsel chipped in efficiently from the field, and Kerry Lyons kept plays alive on the glass and in transition. Pink struggled to find any rhythm outside of Jj Sub, who carried the scoring load nearly by himself in the opening half. Halftime: Gray 39, Pink 35. Pink flipped the script coming out of the half. Matt Riordan found his footing and started attacking downhill, while Jj Sub kept piling on points from all three levels. Pink's defense tightened up, forcing tougher shots and cutting off Gray's second-chance looks. Sub Elizer and Sub Tommy added timely buckets off the bench to keep the pressure on, and Pink outscored Gray 48-40 after the break to complete the turnaround. Pink escaped with an 83-79 road win.

performers.Gray: Matt Spear — 31 pts, 6 REB, 6 AST; Tommy Brockmyre — 21 pts, 8 REB, 1 AST; John Helsel — 18 pts, 8 REB, 1 AST
performers.Pink: JJ — 32 pts, 7 REB, 2 AST; Matt Riordan — 27 pts, 9 REB, 4 AST; Jeromy Anderson — 9 pts, 4 REB

games.text: Green needed every possession it could find. Devin Bradford got White off to a promising start by knocking down triples, and Tyrone Conley was already working the offensive glass. Green answered with Jibril Abdullahi doing a bit of everything, while Joe Sub and Nick Lynn both splashed threes of their own. Green's balance was enough to edge ahead by the break. Halftime: Green 42, White 36. White refused to fold in the second half. Tyrone Conley took over, attacking the rim and cleaning the glass on both ends, while Devin Bradford kept splashing threes to cut into Green's cushion. Green leaned on Abdullahi's do-everything night and Nick Lynn's hot shooting to answer every push, and neither side gave much ground the rest of the way. Green's first-half surge wound up being the difference. Green held off White, 80-74.

performers.White: Tyrone Conley — 29 pts, 17 REB, 3 AST; Devin Bradford — 20 pts, 2 REB, 2 AST; Aid Semic — 9 pts, 8 REB, 1 AST
performers.Green: Jibril Abdullahi — 24 pts, 14 REB, 14 AST; Nick Lynn — 16 pts, 5 REB; Joe Sub — 16 pts, 4 REB, 2 AST

games.text: Orange never trailed. Josh Carter and Stefan Radan set the tone immediately, combining for most of Orange's offense while Kenny Black and Will Ewald controlled the glass. Blue tried to answer behind Logan Letourneau's efficient scoring and Brody Lathrop's outside shooting, but couldn't quite close the gap before the break. Halftime: Orange 45, Blue 41. Blue kept swinging in the second half. Letourneau and Lathrop combined for another big scoring push, and Drew Pelkey added timely buckets to keep Blue within striking distance. But Josh Carter was relentless getting to the free-throw line, and Stefan Radan continued to punish Blue on the boards. Orange matched every Blue run and pushed the lead back out. Orange pulled away for a 92-83 win.

performers.Orange: Josh Carter — 32 pts, 10 REB, 2 AST; Stefan Radan — 30 pts, 11 REB, 6 AST; James Hare — 17 pts, 2 REB, 2 AST
performers.Blue: Logan Letourneau — 25 pts, 3 REB, 2 AST; Brody Lathrop — 19 pts, 3 REB, 2 AST; Drew Pelkey — 13 pts, 7 REB, 1 AST

games.text: Red arrived ready to grind. Jaren Jeffcoat set the tone on the glass immediately, and Tim Lemieux got his scoring going early to help Red build some separation. Black answered with Liam Walsh attacking downhill and Tavarius Vance letting it fly from deep, but couldn't quite catch up before the break. Red led 39-35 at the half. Halftime: Red 39, Black 35. Black clawed its way back into it after the break. Liam Walsh kept scoring in bunches, and Kaleb Swetty found his shot to help even things out. Tavarius Vance stayed aggressive from three, and Andy Sub's playmaking kept Black's offense humming. Black chipped away possession by possession, but Red leaned on Tim Lemieux and Will Oboh to answer every push, and Jaren Jeffcoat kept doing damage on the boards to help Red protect enough of its cushion down the stretch. Red closed it out, 78-75.

performers.Black: Liam Walsh — 21 pts, 6 REB, 1 AST; Tavarius Vance — 17 pts, 6 REB, 2 AST; Kaleb Swetty — 14 pts, 9 REB
performers.Red: Tim Lemieux — 23 pts, 6 REB, 2 AST; Jaren Jeffcoat — 17 pts, 20 REB, 6 AST; Will Oboh — 15 pts, 6 REB, 3 AST
